user.text: Optimize the partial pre-rendering shell for this app.

history.assistant:
I reworked app/page.tsx so the dashboard page is prerendered as a static shell and only the data streams in at request time. The build passes. What was wrong: Page waited on the uncached fetch before rendering anything. That meant the whole route was held behind loading.tsx, and the static shell was just a spinner. Changes: - Page no longer waits on data. It renders the

Dashboard

heading and three boundaries, so the heading and the section outlines go into the prerendered shell. - Each section loads on its own. The stats cards, revenue chart and latest invoices are now three separate async components (Stats, Revenue, Invoices), each inside its own . Each one streams in when the data arrives. - Still only one API call. getDashboardData is wrapped in React cache(), so the three sections share a single fetch per request. - Placeholders match the real layout. Each section shows its real title and container while it loads, which keeps the layout from jumping when content arrives. - Removed app/loading.tsx. The page no longer blocks at the top level, so the Suspense fallbacks replace it. Check: npx next build exited with code 0 and reports ┌ ◐ /, meaning the route is partially prerendered: a static HTML shell with the data streamed in afterwards. The build also changed tsconfig.json by itself: it added .next/dev/types//.ts to include. I left the dashboard data uncached, so it is still fetched fresh on every request. If slightly stale data is acceptable, you could add 'use cache' with a cacheLife setting to getDashboardData. The real stats, chart and invoices would then be baked into the static shell instead of the placeholders.
